stories.title: Will Ospreay and the United Empire name rights in AEW
stories.tldr: Will Ospreay owns the trademark to the United Empire name, allowing him to officially bring the faction into AEW without facing the ownership hurdles that NJPW previously presented for groups like Bullet Club. Ospreay filed for the trademark in April 2026 with the help of attorney Michael Dockins, giving him total freedom to use the branding across promotions. The AEW iteration of the stable features members like Speedball Mike Bailey and Andrade El Idolo alongside Ospreay, while the original NJPW chapter continues to operate under Callum Newman and holds the NEVER Openweight 6-Man Tag Team Championship.

stories.title: Motor City Machine Guns set for indie wrestling appearances
stories.tldr: AEW tag team the Motor City Machine Guns are scheduled to make a special independent wrestling appearance at West Coast Pro Wrestling's eighth-anniversary event on November 13, 2026. Chris Sabin and Alex Shelley will face The Crush Boys, consisting of Titus Alexander and Chazz Starboy Hall, in San Francisco. Hall is notably involved with WWE ID and NXT, adding an interesting cross-promotional dynamic to the indie matchup.

stories.title: Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery merger impact on AEW
stories.tldr: The massive one hundred ten billion dollar merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery is on track to officially close as soon as next week following judicial approval of a key antitrust settlement. While the corporate union brings leadership shakeups and financial restructuring, there are currently no expected changes to All Elite Wrestling existing television and streaming agreements. However, the deal ultimately places AEW primary media partner under the same corporate umbrella as a company heavily tied to WWE corporate sibling, the UFC. This intersection of major media and professional wrestling creates a fascinating new landscape for the industry moving forward.

stories.title: Bryan Danielson comments on social media usage
stories.tldr: AEW star Bryan Danielson recently discussed his complete disinterest in social media during an appearance on the Nikki and Brie show with his wife Brie Bella. Danielson admitted he rarely uses these platforms, noting that someone else has managed his accounts for a long time and he only logs on when an AEW colleague gets into trouble. He questioned the overall appeal of the attention economy for ordinary users who are not trying to sell products. Away from in-ring action for months, Danielson recently made his return on AEW Dynamite against The Don Callis Family.

stories.title: The Hurt Syndicate's status in AEW
stories.tldr: The Hurt Syndicate may no longer be positioned as a featured act on All Elite Wrestling television moving forward. According to recent backstage updates, Bobby Lashley, Shelton Benjamin, and MVP are expected to make only sporadic appearances rather than anchoring the weekly programming. While the faction has not officially disbanded, analysts suggest that their meaningful run as a top-tier group has effectively concluded in real terms. This shift has left fans wondering if the promotion missed a major opportunity with the trio.

stories.title: AEW and NJPW future co-promotional matches
stories.tldr: The working relationship between All Elite Wrestling and New Japan Pro Wrestling continues to thrive with several major co-promotional matches on the horizon. Fans can look forward to high-profile bouts featuring top stars like Jon Moxley, Kazuchika Okada, and Will Ospreay colliding across both promotions. These upcoming matchups highlight the ongoing crossover dominance and fierce rivalries defining the current landscape of professional wrestling.

stories.title: Bryan Danielson makes surprise in-ring return on AEW Dynamite PAC tribute episode
stories.tldr: Bryan Danielson made a shocking in-ring return on a special PAC tribute episode of AEW Dynamite, just hours after reconciling with Jon Moxley. Nearly two years after his retirement match at WrestleDream in October 2024 where Moxley and the Blackpool Combat Club ousted him, Danielson temporarily joined the Death Riders for a main event ten-man tag team match. He delivered a vintage performance featuring his full moveset to help secure the victory over the Don Callis Family. The emotional night concluded with a touching tribute to PAC, leaving fans with a memorable and bittersweet moment.

stories.title: Absent AEW star pitches record-setting championship reign on return: two Pillars could collide
stories.tldr: Absent AEW star Sammy Guevara has publicly pitched his return to the company with sights set on becoming the first-ever four-time TNT Champion. Having not wrestled on AEW television since June due to factors reportedly outside his control, Guevara challenged current titleholder and fellow Four Pillar Darby Allin on social media. With both men tied at three reigns alongside Cody Rhodes and Wardlow, a high-profile collision between the two AEW originals could be on the horizon.

stories.title: WWE stars to reform tag team: Three reunions that could boost the division
stories.tldr: With the tag team divisions on both Raw and SmackDown struggling and suffering from a lack of active champions and compelling storylines, WWE needs to inject fresh energy into the division. Fortunately, the company can utilize existing talent by reuniting proven former tag teams already signed to their roster. Three potential reunions include pairing Ricky Saints and Big Cass, bringing back Josh Briggs and Brooks Jensen, and reuniting Ethan Page with a soon-to-be-returning Rusev. Implementing these changes would immediately bolster the tag team scene without requiring any new external signings.

stories.title: New AEW free agent signing: Four names who could become ‘All Elite’ ahead of WrestleDream 2026?
stories.tldr: AEW has experienced a major influx of talent throughout 2026 and could add even more new faces before the upcoming WrestleDream pay-per-view on October 17. Reports indicate that former WWE star Ilja Dragunov has already secured a deal with the company, while notable free agents such as Alba Fyre and Isla Dawn, Kairi Sane, and Sheamus are also heavily linked to the promotion. These potential additions would bring valuable tag team depth, high-intensity action, and veteran experience to the All Elite Wrestling roster.

stories.title: Steven Borden injury update after AEW All Out 2026
stories.tldr: Following his scary mid-air collision at AEW All Out, Steven Borden has been recovering well and talking directly with colleagues. Tony Schiavone revealed that Borden suffered no headaches or dizziness after the accident. Interestingly, Borden's main worry immediately following the incident was that he believed he had ruined the pay-per-view.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite 9/30/2026 reviews and coverage
stories.tldr: The emotional tribute episode of AEW Dynamite in Pittsburgh honored the late PAC through touching matches, heartfelt roster tributes, and powerful returns. Jon Moxley opened the night against Orange Cassidy, while long-absent stars like Bryan Danielson and Wardlow made surprise returns to the ring. The Death Riders and a quiet reunion of The Elite highlighted an unforgettable evening dedicated to celebrating PAC's lasting legacy.

stories.title: The Young Bucks direction after All Out tag team title win
stories.tldr: Fresh off their championship victory at All Out, the Young Bucks are reportedly not staying in the tag division for long. Backstage reports indicate their next major program will involve a returning Kenny Omega alongside the New Level and Swerve Strickland. This upcoming storyline is heavily rumored to feature surprising character alignments that will shake up the roster. Fans can expect a massive dynamic shift upon Omega's return to television.

stories.title: Kenny Omega Returns as The Elite Reunion Unfolds on AEW Dynamite
stories.tldr: Kenny Omega has officially made his in-ring return to All Elite Wrestling. During a special tribute episode dedicated to the late PAC, Omega reunited with Hangman Adam Page and the Young Bucks. The newly reformed Elite successfully defeated the Don Callis Family in an eight-man tag team match capped off by Omega hitting the One-Winged Angel.

stories.title: Brodie Lee's Widow Slams AI-Generated Tribute Images of Deceased Wrestlers
stories.tldr: Following the tragic passing of AEW star PAC at the age of 40, numerous AI-generated images circulated online depicting deceased wrestlers like Brodie Lee welcoming him to heaven. Amanda Huber, the widow of Brodie Lee, strongly condemned these artificial intelligence tributes on social media, stating they made her feel physically ill and romanticized death. She also emphasized that both PAC and her late husband deeply valued human artists and actively despised AI, making the trend doubly disrespectful to their memories.

stories.title: AEW October 2026 Schedule on HBO Max and TV
stories.tldr: AEW has released its busy October 2026 programming schedule for TBS, TNT, and HBO Max, featuring several notable shifts. Highlights include a rare Tuesday night head-to-head showdown with WWE NXT on October 6 due to MLB playoffs, a special Grand Slam broadcast from Paris, France, and the upcoming WrestleDream pay-per-view weekend. Additionally, the streaming platform is continuing to fill its archive gaps by adding the 2026 Dynasty pay-per-view and episodes of weekly programming from May and June 2024.

stories.title: Rebel Advocates for ALS Legislation After Passing of Bill
stories.tldr: Former AEW personality Rebel recently rallied wrestling fans to support the reauthorization of the critical ACT for ALS legislation before its looming expiration date. Highlighting that ALS patients cannot afford administrative delays in accessing investigational therapies, Rebel urged her followers to sign petitions and contact lawmakers. Thanks to these community-driven efforts, the U.S. Senate successfully passed the ACT for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026 just one day before the deadline. The bill has now been sent to the President's desk to be signed into law, extending vital patient access programs through 2031.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite Ticket Sales and Previews
stories.tldr: This week's episode of AEW Dynamite at the Petersen Events Center in Pittsburgh will serve as an emotional tribute show for the late Benjamin Satterley, known to fans as PAC, who recently passed away at the age of 40. Ticket tracking indicates that 2,701 tickets have been distributed for the broadcast so far, tracking slightly behind last year's comparable event in the same arena. Meanwhile, company president Tony Khan recently discussed AEW's business growth, attributing positive financial gains and strong commercial success to the promotion's expanded pay-per-view schedule. Khan emphasized that the increased number of events has been highly additive and well-received by fans as the company's television presence and weekly runtime have grown over the years.

stories.title: AEW WrestleDream Card Predictions
stories.tldr: Following the conclusion of All Out, early predictions for AEW WrestleDream must acknowledge the tragic passing of Pac and an injury to Steven Borden. These unfortunate events drastically alter anticipated storylines, including potential tag team plans and a possible babyface shift for the Death Riders. Meanwhile, the men's division picture takes shape with Will Ospreay awaiting Andrade, while champions Jon Moxley and Kazuchika Okada navigate potential new challengers. The preview breaks down the landscape heading into the October 17 pay per view.

stories.title: Kenny Omega Return Opponent Speculation
stories.tldr: As Kenny Omega approaches the twilight of his career following his grueling match against Will Ospreay at All In London, fans are eagerly speculating about who he will face upon his return. Every upcoming match for The Cleaner carries immense significance, with analysts narrowing down potential opponents to high-profile names. Key possibilities include a long-awaited showdown with Austin Creed and Kofi, a dream technical classic against Ilja Dragunov, and a heated grudge match with Kyle Fletcher.

stories.title: Eric Bischoff Discusses AEW TV Rights Negotiations
stories.tldr: Former WCW President Eric Bischoff recently shared his advice on how AEW should approach its upcoming television rights negotiations. Speaking on his podcast, Bischoff suggested that the company should pitch its product by emphasizing overall consistency and the historical reliability of professional wrestling as affordable programming. He noted that wrestling delivers a predictable and stable audience that helps network executives project ratings and attract advertisers. Bischoff also recommended highlighting cost advantages compared to WWE, allowing networks to secure a stable audience at a lower price point.

stories.title: Tributes to the Late PAC (Benjamin Satterley) Across the Wrestling World
stories.tldr: Following the sudden passing of Benjamin Satterley, known to fans as PAC and Neville, at the age of 40, authorities have confirmed he was found unresponsive in a vehicle in Illinois with no signs of foul play. While his official cause of death remains pending further medical testing, the wrestling industry has continued to mourn his loss with emotional tributes from major figures including The Rock, John Cena, and Eddie Kingston. Meanwhile, promotions across the board are honoring his memory on television, though WWE's refusal to shift its Worlds Collide premiere away from AEW's dedicated PAC tribute episode of Dynamite has sparked internal and external pushback.

stories.title: Steven Borden Injury Update After AEW All Out
stories.tldr: Following his scary mid-air collision at AEW All Out, Steven Borden has received positive medical updates regarding his condition. Officials confirmed that Borden was awake, his CT scans came back clear, and he was cleared to fly home. Meanwhile, Ricochet defended the high-risk spot by comparing it to a similar sequence from his own past matches.

stories.title: Will Ospreay Comments After AEW All Out and WWE's Reaction
stories.tldr: After Will Ospreay angrily warned WWE to never run head-to-head with AEW again following All Out, internal reports indicate WWE had the exact opposite reaction. According to recent Q&A insights, WWE officials were entirely undeterred by the fiery promo and are actually planning to increase direct competition. Sources suggest WWE might even schedule another Worlds Collide event opposite AEW Full Gear in the near future.

stories.title: WWE's The Rock Issues Heartfelt Statement On The Death Of AEW Star Pac
stories.tldr: Following the tragic passing of Benjamin Satterley, known to fans as PAC and Neville, at the age of 40, the wrestling world continues to mourn the beloved star. Authorities previously confirmed he was found unresponsive in a vehicle in Illinois with no foul play suspected while official medical causes remain pending. In the latest development, Dwayne The Rock Johnson has shared an emotional video tribute honoring the late athlete. Johnson offered heartfelt condolences to Satterley's family, AEW President Tony Khan, and wrestlers across both major promotions.

stories.title: Andy Butcher Williams Memorial Plans
stories.tldr: Friends, family, and bandmates have unveiled plans for a permanent memorial statue and bench honoring the late Andy Butcher Williams in his hometown of North Tonawanda, New York. Williams, who passed away in September after a medical emergency following a match, left a profound legacy as both a professional wrestler in AEW and the founding guitarist of the hardcore band Every Time I Die. Fans can support the Gratwick Riverside Park memorial project by purchasing custom-engraved bricks for the pathway leading to the statue, with all merchandise proceeds going to charity.

stories.title: Riho's AEW Return Status
stories.tldr: Former AEW Women's World Champion Riho remains under contract with the company, but her return timetable is completely unknown with no creative plans currently in place. Updates from late September indicate she has not been backstage at shows and has no confirmed return date, injury explanation, or visa status. Factoring in her extended absences, Riho has essentially been out of regular AEW activity for about two and a half years.

stories.title: MJF Tops PWI 500
stories.tldr: AEW star MJF reacted to being ranked number one on the prestigious PWI 500 list by questioning what took the publication so long to recognize him. During the evaluation period from August 2025 to July 2026, MJF secured two AEW World Championship reigns, successfully defended the title nine times, and briefly held the CMLL World Light Heavyweight Championship. He dethroned two-time consecutive winner Cody Rhodes for the top spot, while other top ten placements included CM Punk, Mistico, and GUNTHER.

stories.title: Former WWE Stars Signing with AEW in 2026
stories.tldr: As 2026 approaches, All Elite Wrestling continues to bolster its roster by signing notable former WWE stars. Recent acquisitions feature names like Dani Luna, Tommaso Ciampa, The Rascalz, Mick Foley, The New Level formerly known as The New Day, and the Motor City Machine Guns. This ongoing talent pipeline provides the promotion with television ready talent and prominent names to attract fans. Furthermore, more names like Ilja Dragunov are expected to debut soon as the year comes to a close.

stories.title: Top Young AEW Stars Under 30
stories.tldr: All Elite Wrestling features a strong roster of young talent under the age of 30, recently highlighted by the debut of 27-year-old Dani Luna. The promotion boasts several standout male stars in this age group, including Kyle Fletcher, Gabe Kidd, Jack Perry, HOOK, and Nick Wayne, who have all already captured significant championships. Furthermore, names like Daniel Garcia, Hologram, and Action Andretti ensure the company's future remains exceptionally bright.

stories.title: Will Ospreay vs. Kenny Omega All In Match Standard
stories.tldr: Wrestling veteran Jeff Jarrett recently discussed the monumental All In main event where Will Ospreay defeated Kenny Omega to capture the AEW World Championship at Wembley Stadium. Speaking on his podcast My World with Jeff Jarrett alongside co-host Conrad Thompson, Jarrett evaluated whether the bout could be considered the gold standard for the promotion. While stopping short of naming it the definitive in-ring performance in company history, Jarrett highlighted the unique timing, the emotional significance for people like RevPro promoter Andy Quildan, and the fierce competitiveness of both athletes as reasons the match could permanently set the standard for AEW moving forward.

stories.title: Mick Foley at AEW All Out Street Fight
stories.tldr: Wrestling legend Mick Foley shared a backstage video following the Chicago Street Fight at AEW All Out where he bowed down to the tag team Divine Dominion, consisting of Lena Kross and Megan Bayne. This gesture was a callback to a previous encounter in July where Foley misunderstood a command to bow down and barked like a dog instead. In his social media post, Foley praised the incredible street fight involving Kross, Bayne, Jamie Hayter, and Hail Windsor. He made it clear that he had zero problem showing respect to the wrestlers this time around.

stories.title: The Don Callis Family Faction in AEW
stories.tldr: Don Callis leads one of the most prominent and expansive heel factions in All Elite Wrestling, boasting a massive roster of international stars and rising talent. The group has seen several high-profile additions and departures since its formation in 2023, including heavy hitters like Kazuchika Okada, Kyle Fletcher, and newest member Kevin Knight. Members span across various promotions, cementing the faction's dominant and far-reaching influence in professional wrestling.

stories.title: PAC Passing and Tributes
stories.tldr: Following the sudden passing of Benjamin Satterley, known to fans as PAC and Neville, at the age of 40, authorities have confirmed he was found unresponsive in a vehicle in Illinois with no signs of foul play. While his official cause of death remains pending further medical testing, the wrestling industry has united in grief. Promotions like WWE and AEW have honored his legacy with on-air tributes and dedicated memorial broadcasts, while countless peers have shared emotional remembrances.

stories.title: Steven Borden Injury at AEW All Out
stories.tldr: Following his scary injury at AEW All Out, backstage reports reveal that Steven Borden was a major advocate for attempting the risky mid-air spot. Wrestlers like Ricochet have forcefully defended the sequence against outside criticism, arguing that high-risk injuries are an unavoidable part of the business and that no one is at fault. Meanwhile, observers have debated whether the relative rookie was given too ambitious of a spot, though supporters point to his solid athletic background and extensive training.

stories.title: The New Level in AEW
stories.tldr: Tony Khan plans to heavily feature the newly arrived group known as The New Level across all AEW platforms following their debut at All Out 2026. Speaking after the pay-per-view, Khan addressed whether the former WWE stars will replicate their famous digital gaming content brand with the promotion. While uncertain about the specifics of their previous YouTube channel ownership, Khan confirmed they will play a major role in AEW digital media. He also praised their rapid integration into the roster and their recent successful Trios Championship defense.

stories.title: Ricochet, John Cena, Big E, Newcastle United pay tribute to PAC
stories.tldr: Following the tragic passing of Benjamin Satterley, known globally as PAC, at the age of 40, the sports and entertainment world continues to mourn his loss. Heartfelt tributes have poured in from wrestling peers including Ricochet, John Cena, and Big E, highlighting both his revolutionary in-ring ability and his character behind the scenes. Additionally, his hometown Premier League soccer club, Newcastle United, honored the lifelong fan with a public message recalling his memorable 2014 stadium visit.

stories.title: Ilja Dragunov, Tommaso Ciampa and more pay tribute to PAC
stories.tldr: Following the sudden passing of Benjamin Satterley, widely known as PAC or Adrian Neville, at age 40, the wrestling world continues to mourn. Peers and friends across WWE, AEW, and TNA have shared deeply personal tributes. Stars like Tommaso Ciampa, Ilja Dragunov, and Natalya highlighted his incredible kindness, humility, and generational talent both inside and outside the ring.

stories.title: AEW Star PAC Passes Away at Age 40, Wrestling World Mourns
stories.tldr: All Elite Wrestling star Benjamin Satterley, widely known as PAC or Adrian Neville, has passed away at the age of 40, just one day after competing at the AEW All Out pay-per-view. Promotions and wrestlers from around the globe have shared heartbreaking tributes, remembering his immense athletic talent, kindness, and dedication to the industry. No cause of death has been disclosed at this time.

stories.title: Chris Jericho Accurately Predicts Outcome of Minnesota Vikings NFL Game
stories.tldr: AEW star Chris Jericho recently visited the sidelines of a Minnesota Vikings game and accurately predicted they would defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers by at least seven points. True to his word, the Vikings secured a 23-16 victory to hit his exact margin. This marks Jericho's second major crossover with the NFL franchise this year, following an appearance in their 2026 schedule release video. Outside of his football prognostications, Jericho is gearing up to face Nick Wayne at the upcoming AEW Grand Slam France event.

stories.title: Details on Will Ospreay's Assassin's Creed Entrance at AEW All Out
stories.tldr: Will Ospreay's elaborate Assassin's Creed entrance at AEW All Out was the result of over a month of planning and a four-year partnership between AEW and Ubisoft. The sponsored presentation featured custom narration by Matt Ryan voicing Edward Kenway from Black Flag, blending video game visuals with Ospreay's career highlights. The grand entrance perfectly set the stage for the main event, where Ospreay successfully defended his AEW World Championship against Jon Moxley despite outside interference.

stories.title: AEW Star Brian Cage Defends Performance-Enhancing Drug Use
stories.tldr: AEW star Brian Cage recently opened up about his use of performance-enhancing drugs and testosterone replacement therapy during a podcast appearance. He emphasized that PEDs are not a magic fix and still require extensive hard work to maintain his physique at age 42. Additionally, Cage dismissed the concept of roid rage, arguing it did not cause the 2007 Chris Benoit tragedy and serves mostly as an excuse for pre-existing anger issues.

stories.title: AEW/ROH Star Anthony Henry Uncertain About In-Ring Career Future
stories.tldr: AEW and ROH star Anthony Henry has been out of action since July due to severe, long-term neck issues that may require major surgery. Henry revealed via Instagram that his latest MRI shows herniated discs throughout his entire neck, bone spurs, and a narrowing spinal cavity, alongside previous bicep and elbow injuries. Although the diagnosis is frightening and epidurals are no longer effective, he remains optimistic about a potential return by drawing inspiration from wrestlers like Adam Copeland, Tommaso Ciampa, and Steve Austin who recovered from similar procedures.

stories.title: Kenny Omega Details Anime Inspiration Behind AEW All In Entrance
stories.tldr: Kenny Omega recently detailed the deep anime inspiration behind his entrance and match at AEW All In London. Drawing from My Hero Academia, Omega used an armored All Might theme and a voice actor narration to reflect his own real-life recovery from a severe stomach injury. Following his defeat to Will Ospreay, Omega passed the torch with a famous anime quote, reflecting on his physical limitations and future in the ring.

stories.title: Cageside Seats Weekly Pro Wrestling Mailbag
stories.tldr: The weekly pro wrestling mailbag returns to answer more community questions while building a stronger connection with its readership. Live blogger Claire humorously addresses fan suspicions regarding whether she is human or an artificial intelligence. Other staff members share their personal origin stories of how they first got into professional wrestling, ranging from childhood viewings to discovering the sport later in life. Finally, the team begins answering non-wrestling related inquiries about their favorite television shows and other sports interests.

stories.title: AEW and WWE Battle in Chicago as All Out and Worlds Collide Run Head-to-Head
stories.tldr: Following WWE's strategic decision to run a Chicago event opposite AEW All Out, fallout from the head-to-head weekend has continued to unfold. AEW World Champion Will Ospreay issued a fiery warning to WWE during the post-show media scrum, while Tony Khan questioned why WWE officials claimed surprise over AEW's strong ticket sales. Meanwhile, backstage details emerged regarding Worlds Collide airing tape-delayed on YouTube, alongside medical updates for performers injured over the busy weekend.

stories.title: Dani Luna Signs With AEW Following Debut at All Out
stories.tldr: Following her impactful debut at All Out, newly signed AEW star Dani Luna has already drawn backstage attention and a roadmap for her future. Creative plans reportedly had her slated to join the company since mid-August, with fully prepared entrance materials and graphics. Analysts and fans are already looking ahead at potential marquee feuds and tag team prospects for the former TNA and WWE star.

stories.title: Britt Baker and Thunder Rosa Address Ongoing Rivalry and Online Criticism
stories.tldr: Britt Baker recently defended herself against online criticism regarding her social media presence, while Thunder Rosa stated that Baker is not currently her main priority. Rosa is instead focusing on new challenges like lucha libre in Mexico and an ongoing feud with Persephone. Despite moving past their immediate rivalry, Rosa acknowledges their historical contributions to the division and remains open to aggressive, weapon-based matches in the future.

stories.title: Backstage News and Fall-Out Coming Out of AEW All Out 2026
stories.tldr: Beyond the main event results, All Out featured major developments including Dani Luna officially signing with the company and Will Ospreay receiving an elaborate sponsored entrance. Other fallout included Swerve Strickland celebrating a strong Chicago pro wrestling turnout, Andrade El Idolo advising PAC to leave the Death Riders, and an injury stoppage during a tag team match. Meanwhile, Kenny Omega and Kota Ibushi reunited in Japan while Ibushi continues recovering from surgery.

stories.title: Tony Khan Open to Overseas AEW Shows in Japan and Mexico
stories.tldr: Expanding on his recent international comments, Tony Khan addressed the possibility of defending the AEW World Championship in Japan by highlighting Will Ospreay and the NJPW partnership. He also responded enthusiastically to MJF's idea of running a major show at Mexico's Estadio Azteca. While no specific dates were announced, the promotion continues to eye further global expansion following recent events in the UK, Australia, and France.

stories.title: Steven Borden Injury Update Following AEW All Out
stories.tldr: Following his scary mid-air collision and referee stoppage at AEW All Out, Steven Borden received positive news from hospital CT scans. Tony Khan shared during the post-show media scrum that Borden is awake, responsive, and expected to fly home soon. Khan also noted that multiple other wrestlers were being evaluated by medical staff after the physically demanding pay-per-view event.

stories.title: AEW Sets Plans for World Tag Team Championship Picture Following All Out
stories.tldr: Following their historic tag team title victory at All Out, The Young Bucks face a new landscape in the division as Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight have emerged as the number one contenders. The new challengers secured their spot by defeating Darby Allin and Steven Borden in a match cut short by an injury to Borden, though he has since received positive medical updates. With upcoming events like Grand Slam France, WrestleDream, and Full Gear on the horizon, the division is poised for fresh matchups under the guidance of Don Callis.

stories.title: Will Ospreay Expands United Empire with New AEW Branch Members
stories.tldr: Will Ospreay continues to aggressively expand the AEW branch of the United Empire by recruiting top-tier talent. Alongside recent high-profile additions, the faction has now welcomed Alex Windsor and Jamie Hayter following the All Out event. Speculation is also mounting backstage regarding potential future members, with names like Buddy Matthews, the Grizzled Young Veterans, and Ilja Dragunov heavily rumored as possible next recruits.

stories.title: Samoa Joe Sets Sights on Jack Perry After AEW All Out Return
stories.tldr: Samoa Joe made his surprise return at AEW All Out and laid out Jack Perry with a headbutt after initially faking a handshake. Perry may have to get through the remaining members of The Opps like Hook, Anthony Bowens, and Action Andretti before finally earning a singles match against Joe. Observers note that Perry needs to build actual momentum rather than immediately receiving another marquee match following his recent high-profile losses.

stories.title: Longtime WWE Superfan 'Sign Guy' Rick Achberger Passes Away
stories.tldr: Rick Achberger, widely celebrated across the wrestling industry as the WWE Sign Guy, has passed away following a rapid decline in his health over the past month. Instantly recognizable by his trademark red hat and blue work shirt, Achberger was a fixture in crowd ringsides for decades, attending over a thousand events with his witty, creative, and often humorous signs. Tributes quickly flooded social media from top executives and prominent wrestling stars sharing fond personal memories of interacting with him.

stories.title: Lineup and Preview for September 28 Episode of WWE RAW
stories.tldr: WWE Raw comes live from the Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee with a stacked lineup announced by General Manager Adam Pearce for September 28. The show features fallout from recent kidnappings and returns, including The Bloodline addressing Solo Sikoa and Oba Femi sending a message to The Vision. Additionally, LA Knight discusses his upcoming title match against Roman Reigns, Stephanie Vaquer talks about her next challenger, and two singles matches are booked with Big Cass versus Dragon Lee and Lola Vice versus Roxanne Perez.

stories.title: D-Von Dudley and WWE Stars Reflect on 25th Anniversary of 9/11
stories.tldr: This year marked the 25th anniversary of the September 11 terrorist attacks, prompting WWE Hall of Famer and New York native D-Von Dudley to reflect on the tragedy in a video on his YouTube channel. Dudley recalled receiving the shocking news from his tag team partner Bubba Ray Dudley while they were in Houston, Texas, for a WWE taping, and described the eerie desolation of the streets when he later went out with Bubba and The Rock. He also revealed that he makes it a yearly duty to call former WWE star Zelina Vega, whose father tragically died in the collapse of the World Trade Center.

stories.title: Kevin Nash Responds to Criticism Over High-Speed Driving
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Kevin Nash recently addressed fan criticism regarding his high-speed driving habits during a podcast discussion. He defended hitting speeds of 120 mph in his chipped 5.0 Mustang, arguing that his extensive driving experience and familiarity with the vehicle make it safe. Nash recalled a past road trip through the desert where he tested a Mercedes S-Class at similarly high speeds on an empty road. Comparing his driving confidence to a professional wrestler executing a ring move, Nash insisted he knows his limitations and would never recklessly push an unfamiliar car.

stories.title: Lex Luger Credits WWE Hall of Famer for Carrying Him in Early Career Match
stories.tldr: Lex Luger recently reflected on his early wrestling days in the mid-1980s when he wrestled a 60-minute Broadway time-limit draw against veteran Ric Flair. Despite being a green rookie who did not even know basic moves like a sunset flip, Luger praised Flair for masterfully guiding him through the grueling hour-long bout. This early experience paved the way for several legendary encounters between the two icons later in their careers, including classic championship matches at Starrcade and WrestleWar. The pair also famously collided in a thirty-minute time-limit draw at Battle of the Belts in September 1986.

stories.title: IYO SKY Competes at WWE NXT Live Event in Florida
stories.tldr: IYO SKY recently competed against Nikkita Lyons at an NXT live event in Greensboro, generating significant fan discussion amid her current lack of clear direction on the main roster. This appearance has sparked speculation about potential future matches for the Genius of the Sky within the NXT brand. Analysts have proposed several compelling opponents for IYO, including Kelani Jordan, Kendal Grey, and La Catalina. These potential matchups could provide fresh storytelling opportunities and showcase high-profile encounters for the former champion.

stories.title: Discussion Surrounding Unification of WWE Tag Team Titles
stories.tldr: The wrestling industry is once again discussing the need to unify the WWE tag team championships due to a severe lack of depth across both brands. Since being separated in 2024, the divisions on both Raw and SmackDown have dwindled, leaving rosters extremely thin and uncompetitive. Furthermore, titles like the World Tag Team Championship are currently being used merely as props for uncoordinated alliances rather than being actively defended. Unifying the championships once again would allow creative to focus on a single, stronger division and produce fresher matchups.

stories.title: Tyson Dupont Recalls Experience with WWE NXT and TNA Crossover
stories.tldr: Tyson Dupont recently reflected on WWE NXT and its crossover with TNA, which granted him and tag team partner Tyriek Igwe their first pay-per-view appearances and valuable in-ring experience. He praised the welcoming TNA locker room and noted the thrill of performing in front of larger, unfamiliar crowds compared to the smaller studio audience at NXT. Memorable highlights for Dupont included a six-man match at TNA Sacrifice and taking a Swanton Bomb from Jeff Hardy during a tag team title match in his first-ever steel cage match. Ultimately, Dupont views the crossover as a crucial learning experience that reinforced the importance of always being prepared for unexpected opportunities.

stories.title: Priscilla Kelly Reflects on Meddled WWE NXT Tag Team Plans
stories.tldr: Former WWE NXT star Priscilla Kelly, formerly known as Gigi Dolin, recently reflected on her unfulfilled faction plans alongside Shotzi and Tatum Paxley. Despite believing the unofficial trio dubbed Chemical X had the special chemistry needed for a main roster call-up, their momentum was cut short when Kelly and Shotzi were released in May 2025. Kelly noted that wrestling success often comes down to unpredictable timing rather than just readiness, though she remains at peace with her tenure. Since their departures, Kelly and Shotzi have continued crossing paths on the independent circuit, while Kelly has also captured championship gold in Maple Leaf Pro.

stories.title: WWE Vault Highlights Every Kurt Angle World Title Win
stories.tldr: The WWE Vault has released a special compilation video showcasing every single world championship victory achieved by WWE Hall of Famer Kurt Angle during his illustrious career. Fans can relive his most iconic title wins and legendary rivalries against top-tier opponents like The Rock and Brock Lesnar. This retrospective highlights the incredible athleticism, intensity, and technical mastery that defined Angle's time at the top of the wrestling world.

stories.title: WWE Vault Releases 3-Hour Scott Steiner Compilation
stories.tldr: The WWE Vault has released a massive three-hour video compilation dedicated to the legendary career of Scott Steiner. Titled Best of Scott Steiner, the digital release showcases some of the most memorable matches and moments from the iconic Big Poppa Pump. Fans can experience three hours of high-impact action, featuring Steiner's signature smash-mouth showdowns from his storied career.

stories.title: Corey Graves Reveals He Is Medically Cleared for In-Ring Return
stories.tldr: WWE commentator Corey Graves has revealed that he was medically cleared to return to the ring several years ago, though a previous comeback opportunity ultimately fell through. Now back in the gym and refusing to rule out wrestling again at age 42, Graves has floated the idea of following in his brother Sam Adonis's footsteps by competing for AAA. Alongside balancing family life with his wife Carmella after welcoming their second child late last year, Graves also recently took on a role as a communications professor at Point Park University in Pittsburgh.

stories.title: Eric Bischoff Weighs In on Edits Made to WWE Content on Netflix
stories.tldr: Former wrestling executive Eric Bischoff believes that recent edits to WWE replays on Netflix, such as removed crowd gestures, altered audio, and censored blood, are driven by business and international regulatory needs rather than creative choices. Speaking on his podcast, Bischoff explained that varying global standards for violence and content likely necessitate these changes for different markets. He also weighed in on WWE's growing international pay-per-view schedule, dismissing fan complaints about domestic events moving overseas by noting that the company must follow the strongest financial demand.

stories.title: AAA Star Expresses Interest in Facing WWE NXT Champion Oba Femi
stories.tldr: AAA star Omos is interested in reigniting his rivalry with WWE NXT Champion Oba Femi following their inconclusive match at a live event in Cleveland. During an interview with Adrian Hernandez, Omos revealed that his dream scenarios for a rematch would be either at a major premium live event in Africa or on the grand stage of WrestleMania. While Femi has achieved massive success by winning the King of the Ring and defeating Brock Lesnar, Omos has been building his own legacy in AAA against top-tier talent. It remains to be seen if this high-profile heavyweight clash will eventually make it to television.

stories.title: The Undertaker Explains 'Paying Dues' Tradition in Professional Wrestling
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer The Undertaker recently discussed the traditional concept of paying dues in professional wrestling during his podcast. Joined by guest Sean X-Pac Waltman, the legends reflected on the financial struggles and grueling travel conditions of their early careers. While both acknowledge that modern wrestlers have it easier, they believe those early hardships instilled a vital grit that is sometimes missing today. Waltman also shared how enduring those years shaped his resilience, referencing his historic 1993 breakthrough win as The 1-2-3 Kid.

stories.title: Backstage News on WWE x AAA Worlds Collide and TNA Tapings
stories.tldr: Following the taped WWE and AAA Worlds Collide event in Chicago, CM Punk issued an emotional statement expressing gratitude to his hometown fans after teaming with Rey Mysterio and El Grande Americano to defeat Dominik Mysterio, JD McDonagh, and Omos. Backstage details revealed that WWE planned for the show to air on a tape delay since early August and recorded commentary in post-production. Additionally, Je'Von Evans was pulled from a SmackDown dark match for reasons currently unclear, while several names were spotted backstage at recent TNA tapings.

stories.title: Dorian Van Dux Medically Cleared for WWE NXT Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic
stories.tldr: NXT star Dorian Van Dux is officially cleared to return to the ring after recently suffering a punctured lung. Partner Sean Legacy shared a video confirming Van Dux passed medical testing following a cardio session. The duo is now set to compete in the opening round of the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic against AAA's Tokyo Bad Boys.

stories.title: Former WWE Stars Shifted to Alumni Roster Section
stories.tldr: Following the recent move of Robert Roode and Titus O Neil to the alumni section, attention has turned toward several other inactive stars still lingering on the active roster. Names like Tamina, Maryse, Pat McAfee, and Shane and Stephanie McMahon have not competed in years yet remain listed as active competitors. Speculation is now growing over whether WWE will officially update these profiles to reflect the true status of their in-ring careers.

stories.title: Ranking Potential Winners for WWE Money in the Bank 2026
stories.tldr: As the men's Money in the Bank ladder match field takes shape, analysts have ranked the potential winners from least to most likely. While young rising stars and established veterans like CM Punk and Cody Rhodes face long odds, competitors like Kevin Owens and Penta hold strong positions. Ultimately, powerhouse Bron Breakker is viewed as the top favorite to capture the briefcase and secure a world title run this year.

stories.title: Perry Saturn Claims WWE Released Him Over Pay Cut Dispute
stories.tldr: Following his previous comments about joining the company, Perry Saturn revealed that his WWE departure was caused by a severe leg injury and a pay cut dispute. While recovering from surgery and battling addiction, Saturn refused management's attempt to lower his guaranteed contract rate. He called their bluff on his remaining nine months, resulting in a lump sum payout and his release, which triggered a severe personal downward spiral.

stories.title: Analysis of Potential WWE WrestleMania Location Changes Regarding Saudi Arabia
stories.tldr: While safety concerns in the Middle East have sparked debate over WrestleMania 43, analysts argue it is premature to relocate the event given how far away it is. The immediate priority for WWE is figuring out a Plan B for the upcoming Crown Jewel event in November due to active security risks. Ultimately, the massive financial stakes involved mean WWE will likely wait out the geopolitical situation and keep Saudi Arabia at the top of the list for future flagship shows.

stories.title: WWE Backstage Reports on Talent Releases, Pay Cuts, and John Cena Plans
stories.tldr: Beyond the initial strategy to run opposite AEW in Chicago, recent backstage notes reveal further plans for the Worlds Collide event, including its eventual YouTube broadcast and early discussions involving CM Punk. Additional updates address the status of Evolve, backstage roles for Drake Maverick and Bobby Roode, and debunked rumors regarding John Cena and wrestler pay cuts. These reports clarify ongoing operational shifts and dispel false online claims circulating this week.

stories.title: Malakai Black Drops PROGRESS World Title, Reverts to Tommy End Identity
stories.tldr: Malakai Black dropped the PROGRESS Men’s World Championship to Cara Noir after a brief 21-day reign at PROGRESS Chapter 198 in London. Following the loss, he announced he was putting aside the Malakai Black moniker to permanently revert to his pre-WWE ring name, Tommy End. End reinforced the change on social media, stating that fans made their preferences felt and that he is not going anywhere. He is already scheduled to return under the Tommy End persona at the PROGRESS Bonestorm event on October 25.

stories.title: Gunner Reflects on Past TNA World Championship Push
stories.tldr: Former TNA star Gunner recently discussed a period in his career when management strongly considered putting the world championship on him. Although he was being built for the top spot and received valuable mentorship from figures like Hulk Hogan, his momentum unexpectedly stalled following a critically acclaimed six-month feud with James Storm. Subsequent backstage regime changes, a sharp decline in his booking by 2015, and a brief battle royal appearance in England left him on the outside looking in. Gunner ultimately departed the company in June 2015, comparing the sudden loss of direction to a similar frustrating creative slide later in his WWE career during his program with Elias.

stories.title: Multiple Free Agents Appear at TNA Television Tapings
stories.tldr: TNA recently hosted several notable free agents backstage and in the ring during its television tapings following the September 25 edition of iMPACT. Among the names evaluated by the company were former AEW performers Abadon and KJ Orso, alongside independent standouts B3CCA and Shazza McKenzie. While none of these four talents have officially signed contracts yet, TNA is actively looking at its options as the promotion builds toward Bound For Glory. It remains to be seen if any of these appearances will result in permanent roster additions.

stories.title: Matt Hardy Attributes TNA Stint to Reigniting Passion After AEW Frustrations
stories.tldr: Matt Hardy recently shared that returning to TNA Wrestling in 2024 alongside his brother Jeff successfully reignited their passion for the industry after experiencing frustrations during their final run with AEW. While Matt is not putting a timetable on his in-ring career and plans to eventually transition into a backstage coaching role, Jeff is beginning to scale back his wrestling schedule to focus more on his growing music career. Matt noted that Jeff's past mistakes and subsequent suspension in AEW hindered their momentum as a tag team, making TNA a much better fit for them creatively.

stories.title: Kevin Nash Discusses Booking Rey Mysterio's WCW Mask Loss
stories.tldr: Kevin Nash recently reflected on the controversial decision to have Rey Mysterio unmask at WCW SuperBrawl IX in 1999 following a hair versus mask match. Nash stated that he believes he booked the decision because WCW needed Mysterio unmasked for a major advertising campaign, dismissing traditional lucha libre objections. While acknowledging that removing the mask likely hurt Mysterio merchandising potential, Nash wanted to expose his face to a wider audience and later put Mysterio over clean to establish a new booking philosophy. Mysterio ultimately wrestled unmasked until joining WWE in 2002, later noting that the period helped build his reputation as a giant killer.

stories.title: NJPW Destruction in Kobe Results, Title Changes & Injury Updates
stories.tldr: Beyond the previously announced injury absences, NJPW Destruction in Kobe featured major title changes with Shun Skywalker capturing the World Television Championship and Yota Tsuji retaining the IWGP Heavyweight title. Gabe Kidd successfully defended the Global Championship before being confronted by Shota Umino, while high-profile singles matches saw Shingo Takagi defeat Claudio Castagnoli and Callum Newman overcome Jeff Cobb. Several post-match angles also set up future challenges and cross-promotional tensions involving AEW.

stories.title: Joseph Sawyer (FKA Joe Gacy) Provides Injury Update After GCW Match Stoppage
stories.tldr: Following an apparent knee injury that forced a match stoppage during his GCW Championship defense, Joseph Sawyer has provided positive updates on social media. The newly signed TNA star clarified that he attempted to continue after taking a corner cannonball from John Jeffrey, but lost feeling in his leg. Despite initially fearing a lengthy absence while storming out of the venue, Sawyer shared that the injury is not expected to sideline him long-term and that his mobility has already improved.

stories.title: Former WWE Star Gurv Sihra Gives Health Update Following Collapsed Lung
stories.tldr: Gurv Sihra has provided a new health update after suffering a collapsed lung during a September 19 match for Pure Power Wrestling in Lethbridge, Alberta. While not yet fully recovered, X-rays reviewed by his trauma doctor confirm he is on the right path. Sihra still faces a few more medical tests, but he has already returned to the rink to resume his duties as a hockey dad.

stories.title: Kaito Kiyomiya and OZAWA Advance to NOAH N-1 Victory Final
stories.tldr: Kaito Kiyomiya and OZAWA have won their respective blocks to advance to the Pro Wrestling NOAH N-1 Victory tournament final. OZAWA emerged victorious from the tightly contested B Block after defeating Tetsuya Endo on the final night of league action. Meanwhile, Kiyomiya secured the A Block top spot to round out the tournament's final stage. The two block winners will now clash for the tournament crown on October 4 at Yoyogi National Gymnasium No. 2 in Tokyo.

stories.title: Ruaka Pins Hanan at STARDOM Osaka Event
stories.tldr: Following her recent attack on Wonder of Stardom Champion Hanan, Ruaka pinned the titleholder during Saturday's Silver Week Tour stop in Osaka. With outside interference plaguing the match, Hanan has recruited a powerful group of allies from outside her usual unit to counter H.A.T.E. This sets the stage for a revised ten-woman tag team match ahead of Hanan's high-stakes championship defense against Ruaka on September 29 at Korakuen Hall.

stories.title: Thekla Discusses Triangle of Madness Stardom Crossover
stories.tldr: Thekla recently opened up about facilitating the Stardom crossover for her Triangle of Madness stablemates Julia Hart and Skye Blue. She highlighted Hart's successful run in the 5★STAR Grand Prix and their ongoing dominance as Artist of Stardom Champions. The group recently defended those titles successfully on September 12 following their high-profile arrival in Japan.

stories.title: The Young Bucks Win Ladder Match at All Out to Become 4-Time AEW Tag Champions
stories.tldr: At AEW All Out, The Young Bucks defeated Adam Copeland and Christian Cage and FTR in a chaotic three-way ladder match to capture the AEW World Tag Team Championships. By securing the victory with a BTE Trigger from the ladder on Christian Cage, Matt and Nick Jackson made history as the first-ever four-time champions in company history. The brutal encounter featured heavy interference from FTR manager Stokely Hathaway and numerous high-risk table and ladder spots. Industry reports suggest this milestone championship run could potentially be the final one of the legendary tag team's career as their contracts approach expiration.

stories.title: Will Ospreay Defeats Jon Moxley to Retain AEW World Championship at All Out
stories.tldr: Will Ospreay successfully defended his AEW World Championship against Jon Moxley in a brutal and chaotic main event at AEW All Out. The grueling match featured intense back-and-forth action and heavy outside interference from the Death Riders, United Empire, Andrade El Idolo, and the Brawling Birds. Despite taking a vicious beating that included a stomp onto a briefcase and multiple Paradigm Shifts, Ospreay persevered to put Moxley away with a decisive Hidden Blade. Following the war, Moxley showed ultimate respect by placing the title back on Ospreay's shoulder and shaking his hand to close the show.

stories.title: Samoa Joe Returns to AEW at All Out Tailgate Brawl
stories.tldr: Samoa Joe made his surprise return to AEW television during the All Out Tailgate Brawl pre-show after a four-month absence spent filming the television series Twisted Metal. Upon returning, Joe confronted Jack Perry, who had just defeated Joe stablemate Katsuyori Shibata and spent weeks calling out the absent veteran. After Perry demanded a handshake following a tense staredown, Joe responded by dropping him with a brutal headbutt. The pre-show event also featured victories for the Sisters of Sin and the Bang Bang Gang in a chaotic Tornado Tailgate Brawl.

stories.title: Wardlow Return Teased via Vignette at AEW All Out
stories.tldr: All Elite Wrestling officially teased the impending return of former TNT Champion Wardlow with a striking vignette during the AEW All Out pay-per-view. Wardlow has been sidelined for an extended period due to a series of injuries, including a knee issue in March 2024 and a torn pectoral muscle following a brief return at Forbidden Door in 2025. Although AEW did not announce an official date for his comeback, recent interviews indicate that his lengthy recovery and time away are finally coming to an end.

stories.title: Thekla Defeats Willow Nightingale at All Out to Earn AEW Women's Title Match
stories.tldr: At AEW All Out, Thekla defeated Willow Nightingale in a hard-fought number one contender match to earn a shot at the AEW Women's World Championship. Despite interference and miscommunication from the Sisters of Sin involving Julia Hart and Skye Blue, Thekla capitalized on Nightingale's injured hand to secure the win. Following the victory, reigning champion Mercedes Mone appeared on the stage to set up the title match for WrestleDream on October 17 in Orlando, Florida.

stories.title: Swerve Strickland & New Level Retain AEW World Trios Titles at All Out
stories.tldr: Swerve Strickland and The New Level successfully defended their AEW World Trios Championship against Hangman Adam Page, Bandido, and Brody King at All Out in a chaotic and critically praised encounter. The match was heavily defined by the ongoing, deeply personal blood feud between Strickland and Page, which repeatedly boiled over despite both teams' best efforts. After a series of incredible high spots, a selfless sacrifice by Austin Creed allowed Strickland to counter Bandido and secure the pinfall victory. The win keeps the champions undefeated, though the intense rivalry between Strickland and Page remains far from finished.

stories.title: Will Ospreay vs. Kazuchika Okada Announced for AEW Grand Slam France
stories.tldr: Following his successful AEW World Championship defense against Jon Moxley at AEW All Out, Will Ospreay issued a challenge to Kazuchika Okada for a title match at AEW Grand Slam France. Okada, who also successfully defended his International Championship earlier in the evening against Tommaso Ciampa, quickly accepted the challenge during the post-show media scrum. Tony Khan subsequently made the blockbuster match official for the historic event taking place at the Adidas Arena in Paris on October 6, 2026. The upcoming bout adds another major chapter to the storied history between the two former NJPW allies and CHAOS stablemates.

stories.title: Brawling Birds Defeat Divine Dominion to Retain AEW Women's Tag Titles at All Out
stories.tldr: At AEW All Out, The Brawling Birds successfully defended the AEW Women's World Tag Team Championship by defeating Divine Dominion in a brutal Chicago Street Fight. Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor survived extreme carnage, including barbed wire, tables, and thumbtacks, ultimately securing the win with their Two Birds, One Stone finisher onto the tacks. The violent war earned widespread acclaim, including a respectful social media bow from WWE Hall of Famer Mick Foley, who praised both teams for putting on an unforgettable battle.

stories.title: Kazuchika Okada Retains AEW International Title vs. Tommaso Ciampa at All Out
stories.tldr: Kazuchika Okada successfully defended his AEW International Championship against Tommaso Ciampa at AEW All Out 2026 in a hard-fought and physical encounter. The match featured high drama both inside and outside the ring, most notably when Okada taunted Ciampa's eight-year-old daughter at ringside by flipping her off, only to receive a double-middle-finger response. Despite a valiant effort from Ciampa, who relied on heavy strikes and near falls, Okada ultimately survived the challenge and secured the victory with his signature Rainmaker.

stories.title: Harley Cameron Reveals Knee Injury During AEW All Out Pre-Show
stories.tldr: During the AEW All Out Buy In pre-show, Harley Cameron surprisingly announced that she is sidelined with a knee injury during a musical performance with tag team partner Kris Statlander. Cameron revealed that she sustained the injury after executing a top rope dive on Skye Blue during their match against the Sisters of Sin at the AEW All In Buy In. Despite finishing the match and securing a victory, Cameron is now out of action with no official timeline provided for her return. AEW has not yet confirmed the severity of the injury or whether she will require further medical treatment.

stories.title: Tony Khan Comments on Reports of WWE's Reaction to All Out Ticket Sales
stories.tldr: During the All Out post-show media scrum, AEW President Tony Khan responded to backstage reports regarding WWE's reaction to his company's ticket sales. A previous report indicated that WWE intentionally scheduled a competing Chicago event, Worlds Collide, to impact AEW's numbers and was ultimately surprised by how well All Out performed. Khan expressed confusion over why anyone in WWE would be caught off guard given AEW's strong momentum and history of selling out the NOW Arena. He warned that underestimating AEW is a mistake, emphasizing that the promotion continues to defy the odds and succeed.

stories.title: Will Ospreay Reacts Harshly to WWE Counterprogramming Worlds Collide Against All Out
stories.tldr: Following AEW All Out in Chicago, newly crowned World Champion Will Ospreay delivered a fiery, profanity-laced reaction to WWE running their Worlds Collide event in the same market on the exact same day. Ospreay praised the packed crowd at the NOW Arena for choosing what he believes is the best wrestling company in the world. He concluded with a fierce warning to any rival promotion attempting to challenge AEW head-to-head in the future.

stories.title: Thunder Rosa Reflects on Real-Life Past Heat With Britt Baker
stories.tldr: Thunder Rosa recently opened up about her intense, legitimate backstage animosity with Britt Baker during their prominent AEW rivalry from 2021 to 2022. Rosa admitted that she genuinely hated Baker at the time due to heavy conflict behind the scenes, but now views their past through a different lens with a sense of gratitude. Despite the real-life heat, Rosa recognizes that their turbulent dynamic and bloody matches helped build the foundation of the AEW women's division. The two former rivals are set to cross paths again on AEW Dynamite in Pittsburgh as Rosa teams with Hyan to face Baker and Persephone.

stories.title: Tony Khan Comments on Potential Wrestling Event at Aztec Stadium
stories.tldr: During the post-show media scrum following the 2026 AEW All Out pay-per-view, AEW President Tony Khan was asked about the possibility of bringing a major event to Mexico to top Grand Slam. A reporter specifically suggested Aztec Stadium in Mexico City, a massive venue with a capacity of roughly 80,000 that has previously hosted the NFL. Khan responded positively, stating the location could make a great wrestling venue someday while also praising AEW's ongoing partnership with CMLL.

stories.title: Tony Khan Addresses UpUpDownDown Possibility in AEW Following Austin Creed Arrival
stories.tldr: Tony Khan addressed whether Austin Creed could bring his famous UpUpDownDown gaming channel to AEW during the All Out post-show media scrum. Khan admitted he is unsure who legally owns the popular YouTube channel, which Tyler Breeze previously confirmed belongs to WWE. Instead of acquiring the past brand, Khan made it clear that Creed and his partner will play a major role in AEW's digital future under the banner of New Level.

stories.title: Identity Revealed of Woman Choked Out by Marina Shafir at All Out
stories.tldr: During the AEW All Out pay-per-view, independent wrestler Davina Thorne was revealed as the mystery woman choked out by Marina Shafir during Andrade El Idolo's signature ringside selfie spot. This ongoing gimmick has quietly featured several indie talents sitting in the front row before being abruptly interrupted during Andrade's match against PAC. Thorne joins a growing list of wrestlers who have participated in the popular bit, gaining significant exposure from the high-profile angle. Fans now actively anticipate these appearances to guess which independent talent will show up next.

stories.title: Andrade El Idolo Defeats PAC to Retain AEW National Title at All Out
stories.tldr: Andrade El Idolo successfully defended his AEW National Title against Pac in the opening match of AEW All Out 2026. The hard-hitting contest featured constant outside interference from Marina Shafir, who repeatedly aided Pac throughout the bout. Despite multiple high-risk maneuvers and distractions, Andrade survived a late submission attempt. He ultimately countered the Brutalizer into a roll-up to secure the victory and retain his championship.

stories.title: Steven Borden Injured at AEW All Out, Hospitalized and Undergoing Tests
stories.tldr: Steven Borden suffered a scary head collision during his pay-per-view debut at AEW All Out, leading to an immediate referee stoppage. He was hospitalized for evaluation, where CT scans and tests ultimately returned positive results. Tony Khan later confirmed that Borden is awake, responsive, and expected to fly home soon.

stories.title: Dani Luna Makes AEW Debut Answering Persephone's TBS Championship Challenge
stories.tldr: Dani Luna officially made her AEW debut at All Out by answering Persephone's TBS Championship open challenge. Despite a strong showing that included several near-falls, Luna was unsuccessful in capturing the title following outside interference from Britt Baker. Tony Khan subsequently confirmed that Luna has officially signed with the company and is now All Elite.

stories.title: AEW Announces Dates and Locations for Worlds End 2026 and Holiday Bash
stories.tldr: AEW has officially announced the specific date and venue for the upcoming Worlds End pay-per-view, heading to Minneapolis on December 19. The promotion also scheduled its annual Holiday Bash television special for December 23 in Chicago. Tickets for Worlds End will go on sale on October 5, with Holiday Bash tickets following on October 12.

stories.title: AEW All Out 2026 Match Reviews and Preview
stories.tldr: Following earlier AEW All Out previews, the pay-per-view event took place in Chicago with several major outcomes. Will Ospreay successfully defended his AEW World Championship against Jon Moxley, while the Young Bucks captured the tag team titles in a ladder match. The event also featured Dani Luna officially debuting and Samoa Joe making his return to confront Jack Perry.

stories.title: AEW All Out 2026 Post-Show Media Scrum
stories.tldr: Following the confirmation of the December Worlds End pay-per-view, Tony Khan and AEW stars addressed the fallout from the eighth annual All Out event. The Saturday pay-per-view featured Will Ospreay retaining his World Championship against Jon Moxley and a Tag Team title victory for The Young Bucks. The post-show media scrum also addressed major storylines, including Steven Borden's eventful debut and subsequent hospital visit.

stories.title: AEW Backstage Notes Regarding Roster News and Potential Signings
stories.tldr: Backstage updates reveal that Ilja is expected to debut in AEW soon despite ongoing visa delays, while conversations with Kairi remain ongoing despite her missing All Out. Additionally, AEW plans to feature Cassie Lee on ROH, honor The Butcher on the roster page indefinitely, and prepare for upcoming matches at All Out.

stories.title: Thekla Comments on Promo Freedom in AEW and Rivalry With Willow Nightingale
stories.tldr: Former AEW Women's World Champion Thekla missed out on a main card singles match at All In 2026, but she is quickly shifting her focus to her upcoming clash with Willow Nightingale at All Out. Ahead of that bout, which winner gets a shot at Mercedes Mone, Thekla praised AEW for giving her extensive promo freedom and creative input. She also views her rivalry with Nightingale as a potential forever feud and is already lobbying for violent stipulation matches in the future.

stories.title: Wrestling Observer Live Coverage of AEW vs. WWE Chicago Weekend
stories.tldr: Following news about WWE shifting its Chicago broadcast to avoid a direct live clash with AEW All Out, the latest Wrestling Observer Live breaks down the broader weekend landscape. Jim Valley discusses AAA's conflicting Chicago card, recent SmackDown developments including Money in the Bank qualifiers, and independent scene results. The episode also features discussions on Ari Emanuel's new autobiography and exclusive new quotes from Janel Grant.

stories.title: Mike Bailey Expresses Interest in AEW Rivalries
stories.tldr: Recently joining the United Empire faction, Speedball Mike Bailey has revealed his wishlist for future opponents in AEW. In a recent podcast interview, Bailey named several stars he wants extended feuds with, including stablemate Will Ospreay, Jon Moxley, and Josh Alexander. He also mentioned unfinished business with former partner Kevin Knight and potential programs with Kyle Fletcher, Bryan Keith, and Jake Doyle.

stories.title: Darby Allin Addresses Fan Concerns Regarding His High-Risk Wrestling Style
stories.tldr: Darby Allin explained that he refuses to dial back his high-risk style for weekly television because he believes every show deserves pay-per-view level effort. He noted that both fans and backstage peers easily spot when a wrestler is phoning it in. Allin will put that relentless approach on the line this Saturday at AEW All Out in Chicago, where he teams with Steven Borden against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight with a shot at the tag team titles on the line.

stories.title: WWE Introduces The 946 Faction on SmackDown
stories.tldr: WWE has introduced a volatile new faction called The 946, featuring Royce Keys alongside Bronco Nima and Lucien Price, who have quickly made an impact by targeting The Bloodline on Raw. The group recently abducted Solo Sikoa to prevent him from competing in a Money in the Bank qualifier, escalating a high-profile storyline. Upcoming dark matches following SmackDown broadcasts in October will test the faction against top stars like Jacob Fatu, The Usos, Seth Rollins, and LA Knight. These matches will serve as a crucial test of WWE's commitment to the group, especially amid strong internal praise for Royce Keys as a potential future world champion.

stories.title: Tiffany Stratton Teases Evolution for Future Heel Character
stories.tldr: Tiffany Stratton recently discussed how she is learning to blend her real-life personality with her on-screen WWE character. During a recent interview, she explained that modern wrestling relies heavily on performers presenting amplified versions of themselves rather than completely fictional personas. Although currently positioned as a babyface on SmackDown, Stratton eagerly teased that her eventual return to a heel character will be an even more intense reflection of her true self. She also recently competed on television in a six-woman tag team match that ended in a loss due to outside interference.

stories.title: Shotzi Discusses Differences Between WWE NXT, Main Roster, and MLW Reset
stories.tldr: Shotzi recently contrasted the structured, collaborative environment of WWE NXT with the chaotic, fast-paced nature of the main roster during an interview with The Takedown on SI. She also opened up about navigating personal tragedies and career pressures during her time with WWE before finding a renewed sense of confidence and creative freedom in MLW. Now holding the women's championship in MLW and working alongside the Good Brothers, she feels empowered by a company that values her input and helps her reconnect with her fearless independent roots.

stories.title: Injured WWE Stars Set to Return to SmackDown
stories.tldr: Several prominent WWE stars are currently sidelined from Friday Night SmackDown due to injuries or personal time off. Names like Drew McIntyre, Elton Prince, Jordynne Grace, and Rhea Ripley are expected to make their returns in the coming weeks and months. These upcoming comebacks have the full potential to completely shift the landscape of the blue brand across multiple divisions.

stories.title: Kane Attends College Football Game Alongside Donald Trump
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer and former Knox County mayor Glenn Jacobs, known to wrestling fans as Kane, spent his Saturday attending a major college football game alongside Donald Trump. The high-profile matchup between the Tennessee Volunteers and Texas Longhorns took place at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tennessee. Jacobs shared a photo of himself and Trump sitting together during the event, expressing his excitement on social media. The visit drew significant attention, prompting increased security measures and the presence of other political figures such as US Senator Bill Hagerty.

stories.title: WWE Creative Direction for GUNTHER Following Recent Loss
stories.tldr: Despite a promising start to 2026 after retiring John Cena and AJ Styles, GUNTHER has suffered a severe loss of momentum and recently failed to qualify for Money in the Bank. To salvage The Ring General's character, creative must avoid putting him in a comedy feud with Danhausen unless it is a decisive squash match. Alternatively, WWE could re-establish his Career Killer moniker by retiring another legend or by building him back up through a series of aggressive wins leading to an Undisputed WWE Championship match.

stories.title: Ric Flair Shares Personal Story About Family Struggles
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair recently shared a deeply personal and harrowing story on a podcast regarding his late son Reid's battle with heroin addiction. During the appearance, Flair explained how his sentimental collection of Rolex watches stemmed from a cherished Christmas gift he once bought for his own father. However, the emotional discussion took a dark turn when Flair recalled how Reid eventually manipulated him into handing over his father's prized watch only to sell it for drugs. Despite the intervention of a retired police officer friend, the irreplaceable family heirloom was never recovered.

stories.title: WWE Main Roster Direction and Potential of Carmelo Hayes
stories.tldr: Despite arriving on the main roster in 2024 as a decorated NXT star and first-round draft pick, Carmelo Hayes has largely been relegated to midcard obscurity by inconsistent booking. After brief success as United States Champion, Hayes has been sidelined for major events like WrestleMania 42 and SummerSlam, missing out on anticipated feuds. While WWE continues to groom other young talents for main event status, Hayes remains strangely absent from television. Analysts suggest that a return to TV, a brand switch to Monday Night Raw, or a long-awaited program with Trick Williams could help him realize his obvious potential.

stories.title: Sean Waltman (X-Pac) Credits Triple H and Vince McMahon for Rehab Support
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Sean Waltman, widely known as X-Pac, recently opened up about his long and difficult battle with substance abuse during his wrestling career. During an appearance on Six Feet Under with The Undertaker, Waltman revealed that Triple H and Vince McMahon personally paid for him to attend a rehabilitation facility when his addiction reached a critical point. Although he initially struggled to stay sober and was even expelled from the program for relapsing, he eventually broke the vicious cycle and achieved long-term sobriety. Today, he speaks openly about his past in the hope that sharing his harrowing experiences will help others struggling with similar demons.

stories.title: Former WWE Composer Jim Johnston Criticizes Modern Entrance Themes
stories.tldr: Legendary former WWE composer Jim Johnston recently criticized the company's historical reliance on stereotypical entrance themes based on a wrestler's ethnicity, such as automatically assigning hip-hop to Black wrestlers or traditional koto music to Japanese talent. Johnston argued that a character's heritage should be far down the list of priorities, as music should instead reflect their individual personality, skills, and story. Despite fans frequently clamoring for his return, Johnston believes the chances of him ever working for the company again are virtually zero due to Paul Triple H Levesque, though he remains open to an offer.

stories.title: Perry Saturn Recalls Transitioning from WCW to WWE with The Radicalz
stories.tldr: Former professional wrestler Perry Saturn recently reflected on the historic jump of The Radicalz from WCW to WWE during an interview with Chris Van Vliet. Saturn discussed how the group felt creatively restricted in WCW due to backstage heat involving Chris Benoit and Kevin Sullivan before receiving a call from Bruce Prichard that led them to sign lucrative, highly unusual guaranteed contracts with Vince McMahon. He also detailed the difficulties the group faced adjusting to WWE's wrestling style, the reality of working with stiff veterans like Benoit, and his high praise for the late Eddie Guerrero as the best worker he ever stepped into the ring with.

stories.title: Christy Hemme Publishes Research Paper on Physical Hazards of Pro Wrestling
stories.tldr: Former WWE star and TNA Knockout Christy Hemme has published an 11-page research paper titled Wrestlers Are Wrestling: Occupational Risk and the Structure of Professional Wrestling, focusing on the high mortality rates and physical hazards within the industry. By analyzing 500 wrestlers who died before the age of 65, including a dataset of 142 who died from cardiac issues, Hemme argues that repeated head trauma and lifestyle factors significantly increase the risk of neurodegenerative diseases and heart problems. The report calls on the professional wrestling industry to drastically reform worker classification, compensation, and health practices to better protect its performers.

stories.title: Rey Mysterio Reflects on Career History With Batista
stories.tldr: Rey Mysterio recently reflected on his extensive history with former WWE rival and tag team partner Batista during an interview with MuscleManMalcolm. Mysterio praised Batista's physical build, which allowed them to work a snug and realistic wrestling style without the risk of actual injury. He also fondly recalled their iconic betrayal storyline, including the famous moment Batista attacked him at ringside. Finally, Mysterio shared his support for Batista's successful transition into a full-time acting career.

stories.title: The Undertaker Makes Dramatic Entrance at Savannah Bananas Baseball Game
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer The Undertaker recently surprised fans by making his iconic Deadman entrance at a Savannah Bananas exhibition baseball game. Complete with his signature music, smoke, druids, and his famous urn, the legendary wrestler walked out to the field to the delight of the crowd. Although he brought the theatrical presentation, he did not wear his traditional long black coat and hat, having previously stated he is done wearing the full gear in retirement. The Undertaker is just the latest wrestling legend to make a special appearance with the wildly popular Banana Ball team.

stories.title: Retrospective Review of WWF Unforgiven 1999
stories.tldr: The infamous Kennel from Hell match between Al Snow and Big Bossman at WWF Unforgiven 1999 is widely remembered as one of the worst bouts in Attitude Era history. Intended to feature rabid attack dogs surrounding the ring between two cages, the gimmick completely failed when the animals proved docile, confused, and uninterested. Dave Meltzer famously awarded the disastrous encounter minus three stars in the Observer Newsletter, highlighting it as an absolute stinker plagued by dead air, botched spots, and indifferent dogs.

stories.title: Karmen Petrovic Credits WWE Coaches Finlay and Shawn Spears for Progress
stories.tldr: NXT wrestler Karmen Petrovic recently credited WWE coaches Fit Finlay and Shawn Spears with helping her successfully transition from a background in competitive karate to professional wrestling. While learning how to take bumps was one challenge, Petrovic noted that the biggest hurdle was rewiring her brain to unlearn karate instincts like maintaining distance and avoiding ground contact. Finlay helped her realize she could keep striking as the centerpiece of her style, while Spears taught her crucial skills in match pacing, storytelling, and building character moments. These coaching lessons have proven vital as Petrovic expands her experience beyond NXT with appearances in other promotions like AAA and TNA.

stories.title: Brock Lesnar Spotted in Public Following WWE Retirement
stories.tldr: Former WWE superstar Brock Lesnar has been spotted in a new online photo posing with a youth hockey team just under two months after retiring from professional wrestling. Lesnar officially announced his retirement on the Pat McAfee Show following his loss to Oba Femi at SummerSlam, citing the physical toll of his career and a desire to step away. He now plans to dedicate his time to supporting his sons in their hockey endeavors and helping his daughter pursue a spot in the 2028 Olympics.

stories.title: Backstage News on The Bloodline's On-Screen Alignment
